newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, but gains expected.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, but gains expected.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.28 percent on Friday, ending the week 2.4 percent lower, but traders said gains would resume as early as next week.
They said strong interest among domestic and foreign investors in newly-privatised companies was expected to push up the index significantly in the next two and a half months.
"The index could gain up to 20 percent by the end of the year," one trader said. Since September 10, the SBI index has risen 42.2 percent.
Overall 11 shares fell, five rose and one kept steady, while seven were untraded.
Bank SKB was most actively traded, falling 3.99 percent to 40,710 tolars on volume of 5,437 shares for total turnover of 225.5 million tolars.
Preferred shares of bank Dolenjska banka were the leading decliners. They fell 4.61 percent to 12,830 on volume of 65 shares for total turnover of 1.6 million tolars.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the top gainer, rising 6.56 percent to 26,000 on volume of 100 shares for total turnover of 2.6 million tolars.
